newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS to adopt IAS for 1997 annual accounts.
newsitem.headline: UBS to adopt IAS for 1997 annual accounts.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS), Switzerland's largest bank, said its annual accounts for 1997 would be reported according to the International Accounting Standards (IAS).
UBS said in its half-year statement that this should lead to increased transparency, further international credibility and improved international comparability.
The motive for the decision by the board of directors was "to constantly improve the transparency of its finanical information and to create a basis for international comparison."
UBS will also restate its 1996 accounts for comparison purposes, a UBS spokeswoman said.

UBS said its current practice of combining Swiss accounting rules with an adapted version of European Union directives is no longer adequate to meet today's requirements when multinational companies are increasing opting for internationally accepted standards.

"We have chosen IAS because it enjoys broad acceptance throughout the world as an internationally established system of accounting rules which incorporates the changing needs of financial reporting on an ongoing basis," UBS said.
